Bill.BriefDescription: Regarding vision screening for public school students.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to vision screening of school children; amendingRCW 28A.210.020; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature recognizes that, among othercauses, students who, from one semester to the next, exhibit strikingbehavior or discipline changes or a sudden drop in academic performancemay have vision impairments. It is the goal of the legislature that,to the extent that funds are available, such children be givenadditional vision screening.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 28A.210.020 and 1971 c 32 s 2 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Every board of school directors shall have the power, and it shallbe its duty to provide for and require screening for the visual andauditory acuity of all children attending schools in their districts toascertain which if any of such children have defects sufficient toretard them in their studies. Auditory and visual screening shall bemade in accordance with procedures and standards adopted by rule ((orregulation)) of the state board of health. Those students who exhibit p. 1 SB 5958a striking behavior or discipline change, or a sudden drop in academicperformance may be subject to additional visual screening in order todetermine whether the change in behavior, discipline, or grades is dueto visual impairment. Personnel conducting the additional visualscreening shall use a functional vision test in addition to screeningrequired by the state board of health. Prior to the adoption orrevision of such rules ((or regulations)) the state board of healthshall seek the recommendations of the superintendent of publicinstruction regarding the administration of visual and auditoryscreening and the qualifications of persons competent to administersuch screening.
